prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part for B042 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case. It showed that the five other members reached the same trio from different starting points, and Linnarsson moved to it for reasons he stated, not for the sake of agreement. The chain from proglucagon processing and the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, through human incretin physiology and receptor biology, to agonists with randomized evidence in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes, is complete, independently confirmed over decades and still expanding. The discovery is a physiological one about a gut hormone, and a citation can be written around the hormone and its active form without naming a drug. I also see no second prize part that would improve the prize. Every candidate that was named as an alternative has a larger attribution gap than B042, or a maturity or tool-versus-discovery question that the committee has not resolved, and adding a second part would force the GLP-1 credit below three names, which would make the weakest point of B042 worse.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and the round-1 exchange has not removed it. Mojsov's priority over the Habener group for the active peptide is a recollection shared by several of us and not a checked record, and a prize that names her has to be defensible on the primary literature. Knudsen's engineering of long-acting agonists was not routine, and her omission is a real cost that I would want recorded in the committee's reasoning and not treated as a clean exclusion. The citation also carries a risk. If it reads as honouring a drug class, it undercuts the argument for the trio, and if it reads as slighting the drug design, it understates the medical achievement. Long-term durability of weight loss and long-term safety are still accumulating, though this does not affect the mechanistic discovery.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius argues that attribution uncertainty should not push B042 below B038 or B013, since their credit lists have comparable gaps (Eshhar for CAR-T, Zhou for the HPV particles), and that the GLP-1 gaps are narrower than my round-1 caution implied.
responses.response: I accept the comparison and it has shifted my reading. My round-1 caution on B042 was not meant to rank it below B038 or B013 and I do not do so. The gaps differ in kind. For B042 the open question is a contested priority between two groups over one step in a chain whose other links are firm, and a fallback exists in Knudsen. For B038 Eshhar's concept lies outside the credited names and Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer may be a separate achievement from CAR engineering, so the credited trio is not one coherent story. For B013 the relation to the 2008 HPV prize and Zhou's deceased status are open and cannot be repaired by choosing a different name. I therefore consider the B042 gap the narrowest of the three, which is why I keep it as the single part.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from a Knudsen-inclusive trio to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, accepts the trio as the most coherent set and not the only fair one, and holds that Knudsen should replace Mojsov if the discovery case is judged to rest on the therapeutic step.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of this position and with his reason for moving. Where I qualify it is on the trigger for the fallback. The committee should not swap Knudsen in simply because the Mojsov-Habener priority is uncomfortable. It should do so only if the record shows that Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active form is not distinguishable from proglucagon cloning and sequence work, because otherwise we would be replacing a discoverer with a developer to avoid a hard question. On what I can reconstruct without the sources in front of me, Mojsov's work on synthesising and characterising GLP-1(7-36) amide and showing that it is the insulinotropic form is separable from proglucagon cloning, and I would defend naming her on that basis. I state this as recollection that remains to be verified.

responses.point: Perlmann warns that agreement among members on the same trio must not turn a recollection of the priority history into settled fact, and asks which of the three basic contributors the committee would drop if the translational step had to be represented.
responses.response: That warning is right and applies to me as much as to anyone. I cannot say the trio is uncontested, and the citation should therefore be worded on the physiology and the identification of the active form and should not assert who was first. On his question, I would not drop Holst or Drucker. Holst's human incretin physiology and Drucker's receptor biology and translation are the two least disputed contributions. The only name that could responsibly come out is the one with a disputed priority, and in that case Knudsen would take the place. I would not frame it as cutting a basic contributor for a developer in general.

responses.point: El-Manira asks that the tool-versus-discovery question be answered once and applied consistently to B004 and B029, and he places B029 close to his own field and flags that for care.
responses.response: I think the principle can be stated plainly. A tool belongs on a prize shortlist only if it opened a new class of biological discovery, or if its medical consequence is already demonstrated. B029 meets the first test strongly, and I said in round 1 that its neuroscience case is stronger than my own ranking implied. B004 meets both. Neither is excluded as a tool. The reason B029 does not compete with B042 for the prize this year is the attribution cap, since six credited names cannot be cut to three without excluding Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck, and not a categorical objection to tools. I would apply the same attribution test to B004, where the credited trio is also narrower than the history of the technology.

responses.point: Sandberg-Rickard notes that a topic as widely known as B042 may be treated as the default and receive less scrutiny than lower-ranked candidates.
responses.response: I agree with this concern, and it is why I reread the alternatives before settling. B038 has the strongest basic claim among them, but the unresolved Eshhar and Rosenberg questions mean that it would need a cleaner attribution than the one in front of us. B013 has an established mechanism and a clear clinical effect, but its link to the 2008 prize and Zhou's position are not resolved. After this check B042 still stands on the science and not on familiarity. If it were not unanimous at opening, I would still arrive at the same trio.

uncertainties: Whether the record, once checked against primary sources, supports naming Mojsov for the active peptide and not Habener, and whether Knudsen should replace her if it does not.
Whether the B042 citation can acknowledge incretin-based treatment without implying that the committee has adjudicated the Mojsov and Habener priority question.
Whether Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer should be treated as a separate achievement from CAR engineering in B038, and how Eshhar's omission affects it as a future candidate.
How B013 relates to the 2008 HPV prize and how Jian Zhou's deceased status is handled.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I worked with Paul Greengard during my postdoctoral period and have around twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy. Neither relationship involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, so I see no ground for recusal. Round 1 raised no new conflict that bears on B042, B038 or B013.
